quests.hint: BENE- means 'good.' VOL means 'will' or 'wish.' -ENT forms an adjective. Which prefix fits a word describing someone who wishes others well and acts with kindness?
quests.explanation: BENE- ('good') + VOL ('will') + -ENT = BENEVOLENT, describing someone who wishes others well and acts with kindness and generosity.
quests.meaningBreakdown: BENE (prefix, 'good') + VOL (root, 'will') + ENT (suffix, forms an adjective)
quests.instruction: Use the pieces you know: BENE- means 'good,' VOL means 'will.' Which prefix fits this description?

quests.hint: A cartoon villain who takes pleasure in causing others harm and plots against the hero at every turn.
quests.explanation: MALEVOLENT is MALE- ('bad') + VOL ('will') + -ENT, describing someone who wishes harm on others — the direct opposite of BENEVOLENT.
quests.meaningBreakdown: MALE (prefix, 'bad') + VOL (root, 'will') + ENT (suffix, forms an adjective)
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: A sudden sneeze or a knee-jerk reflex — something your body does without you consciously choosing it.
quests.explanation: IN- ('not') + VOLUNT ('will/choice') + -ARY = INVOLUNTARY, happening without conscious control or choice. You already know VOLUNTARY (done by free will) from earlier — this is its logical opposite.
quests.instruction: Which prefix negates VOLUNTARY to describe an action with no conscious choice involved?

quests.hint: BENE- means 'good.' FIC relates to 'making' or 'doing.' Which word describes vitamins that genuinely improve your health?
quests.explanation: BENEFICIAL is BENE- ('good') + FIC ('doing/making') + -IAL, producing good effects or results.
quests.meaningBreakdown: BENE (prefix, 'good') + FIC (root, 'doing/making') + IAL (suffix, 'having the quality of')
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation, using what BENE- means?

quests.hint: A smoke detector that suddenly stops beeping during a fire because a wire came loose inside.
quests.explanation: MALFUNCTION is MAL- ('bad') + FUNCTION, to fail to work correctly or as intended.
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: A surgeon operates on the wrong leg due to carelessness, and the hospital faces a lawsuit as a result.
quests.explanation: MAL- + PRACTICE = MALPRACTICE, improper or negligent professional conduct, especially by a doctor or lawyer. BENE- would instead describe good conduct, the opposite situation entirely.
quests.instruction: BENE- means 'good.' MAL- means 'bad.' Which fits this situation?

quests.hint: INTRO- means 'inward.' VERT means 'turn.' Which word describes someone who recharges by spending quiet time alone rather than at a big party?
quests.explanation: INTROVERT is INTRO- ('inward') + VERT ('turn'), someone whose energy and focus turn inward, toward their own thoughts.
quests.instruction: Use the pieces you know: INTRO- means 'inward.' Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: Someone who feels energized after a night out talking to dozens of new people at a crowded party.
quests.explanation: EXTROVERT is EXTRO- ('outward') + VERT ('turn'), someone whose energy and focus turn outward, toward other people — the opposite of an INTROVERT.
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: A barn that gets completely redesigned and turned into a cozy guest house.
quests.explanation: CON- ('together/completely') + VERT ('turn') = CONVERT, to change something completely from one form or use into another. INTRO- would instead mean turning inward, which doesn't fit a building changing purpose.
quests.instruction: Which prefix correctly completes this word?

quests.hint: INTRO- means 'inward, into.' DUCE means 'lead.' Which word describes bringing a new coworker into the office and telling everyone their name for the first time?
quests.explanation: INTRODUCE is INTRO- ('into') + DUCE ('lead'), to lead or bring someone or something into a new situation.
quests.instruction: Use the pieces you know: INTRO- means 'into.' Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: An orchestra leader stands at the front, waving a baton to guide dozens of musicians playing together in time.
quests.explanation: CONDUCT is CON- ('together') + DUCT ('lead'), to lead or guide a group, as in leading an orchestra.
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: A company cuts its workforce from 500 employees down to 350 to save money during a slow year.
quests.explanation: RE- ('back') + DUCE ('lead') = REDUCE, to lead something back to a smaller size or amount. INTRO- would instead mean bringing something in, not shrinking it — a completely different direction.
quests.instruction: Which prefix correctly completes this word?

quests.hint: PRO- means 'forward.' SPECT means 'look.' Which word describes the likely future outcome a business plan is aiming for?
quests.explanation: PROSPECT is PRO- ('forward') + SPECT ('look'), a possibility or expectation for the future — literally, a look ahead.
quests.instruction: Use the pieces you know: PRO- means 'forward.' Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: A building safety officer walks through every floor, checking wiring, fire exits, and smoke detectors before approving the site.
quests.explanation: INSPECT is IN- ('into') + SPECT ('look'), to look closely into something to check its condition or quality.
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: After a difficult year, someone spends a quiet weekend alone journaling and reflecting on their own choices and values.
quests.explanation: INTRO- ('inward') + SPECT ('look') = INTROSPECT, to look inward and examine one's own thoughts and feelings. PRO- would instead mean looking forward, toward the future — a different direction of attention entirely.
quests.instruction: Which prefix correctly completes this word?

quests.hint: DE- means 'away, down.' PORT means 'carry.' Which word describes a government forcibly sending someone out of the country?
quests.explanation: DEPORT is DE- ('away') + PORT ('carry'), to carry or send someone away from a country, usually by legal order.
quests.instruction: Use the pieces you know: DE- means 'away.' Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: A grocery store sells bananas, coffee, and mangoes that were all grown in other countries and shipped in.
quests.explanation: IMPORT is IM- ('into') + PORT ('carry'), to carry goods into a country from somewhere else.
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: A charity raises funds to help pay a struggling family's rent and groceries during a hard year.
quests.explanation: SUP- (a form of SUB-, 'under') + PORT ('carry') = SUPPORT, to carry or hold something up from underneath — literally or figuratively, as in providing help. IM- would instead mean bringing goods into a country, a totally different context.
quests.instruction: Which prefix correctly completes this word?

quests.hint: DE- here means 'down, fully.' SCRIBE means 'write.' Which word describes putting into words exactly what a suspect looked like for a police sketch?
quests.explanation: DESCRIBE is DE- ('fully/down') + SCRIBE ('write'), to give a detailed account of something in words.
quests.instruction: Use the pieces you know: SCRIBE means 'write.' Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: A jeweler carefully engraves the couple's wedding date directly into the inside of a gold ring.
quests.explanation: INSCRIBE is IN- ('into') + SCRIBE ('write'), to write or carve words directly onto or into a surface.
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: A handwritten note added below the signature at the end of a letter, right after 'Sincerely.'
quests.explanation: POST- ('after') + SCRIPT ('write') = POSTSCRIPT, literally 'written after,' the extra note added at the end of a letter. This reviews POST- from earlier and shows it can combine with a brand-new root just as easily as with GRADUATE or SEASON.
quests.instruction: Which prefix correctly completes this word?

quests.hint: IN- here means 'upon, into action.' VOKE means 'call.' Which word describes a judge calling upon an old law to justify a ruling?
quests.explanation: INVOKE is IN- ('upon') + VOKE ('call'), to call upon or appeal to something, like a law, rule, or higher power.
quests.instruction: Use the pieces you know: VOKE means 'call.' Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: After too many speeding tickets, the DMV takes away a driver's license entirely.
quests.explanation: REVOKE is RE- ('back') + VOKE ('call'), to call something back, canceling a right or privilege that was previously granted.
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: A nurse describes her career not just as a paycheck, but as something she felt genuinely called to do since childhood.
quests.explanation: VOCATION comes from the same root as INVOKE and REVOKE — VOC/VOKE, meaning 'call.' A VOCATION is literally a 'calling,' a profession someone feels deeply drawn to. Recognizing the shared root across INVOKE, REVOKE, and VOCATION is exactly the inference skill this phase is building.
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: RE- means 'back.' PORT means 'carry.' Which word describes carrying information back to your boss after finishing an assignment?
quests.explanation: REPORT is RE- ('back') + PORT ('carry'), to carry information back to someone, or to give an account of something.
quests.instruction: Use the pieces you know: RE- means 'back.' Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: A doctor writes out exactly which medication and dosage a patient should take, before they even leave the office.
quests.explanation: PRESCRIBE is PRE- ('before') + SCRIBE ('write'), to write out instructions or recommendations in advance, especially for medicine.
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: A heckler in the crowd keeps shouting insults, clearly trying to get a reaction out of the performer on stage.
quests.explanation: PRO- ('forth') + VOKE ('call') = PROVOKE, to call forth a reaction, usually anger or irritation, deliberately. IN- would instead mean calling upon something formally, like a law — a much calmer, more official action.
quests.instruction: Which prefix correctly completes this word?

quests.hint: A priest offers a closing blessing at the end of a wedding ceremony, wishing the couple well.
quests.explanation: BENEDICTION is BENE- ('good') + DICT ('say') + -ION, literally 'a good saying' — a blessing. This checkpoint reviews BENE-/MAL- alongside DICT, the same root you met all the way back in PREDICT.
quests.meaningBreakdown: BENE (prefix, 'good') + DICT (root, 'say') + ION (suffix, forms a noun)
quests.instruction: Checkpoint: which prefix means 'good'?

quests.hint: A detour sign sends traffic away from the closed highway and onto a side road instead.
quests.explanation: DIVERT uses a form of DIS- ('away/apart') combined with VERT ('turn'), to turn something away from its original path. This checkpoint reviews the VERT family: INTROVERT, EXTROVERT, CONVERT, and now DIVERT — all built from the same 'turn' root.
quests.instruction: Checkpoint: which prefix means 'away, apart'?

quests.hint: Looking back on a decision made years ago, with the benefit of everything you've learned since.
quests.explanation: RETRO- means 'backward,' a new prefix, but you already know SPECT means 'look' from PROSPECT and INTROSPECT. RETROSPECT is literally 'looking back.' Meeting a brand-new prefix attached to a root you already know, and figuring out the meaning anyway, is exactly what this phase has trained you to do.
quests.instruction: Checkpoint: this word uses a prefix you haven't seen before. Can you infer its meaning from the context?
